main_body: A three-storey red-brick building drawn as a flat green rooftop with a parapet above a brick facade with window rows, a cornice and an arched green double door.
top_band: Rows 1-5 light grey parapet, then green roof surface (L~115-155) rows 7-38, then a light edge at rows 39-41, with cream dentil cornice rows 42-46 above dark brick
evidence: The scan at x=80 shows the parapet (L 226/181/158), then green roof rows 8-38 with a vent and hatch drawn on it so it reads as a horizontal surface. Rows 39-41 are a light front-edge line (L 235/205). Cream cornice rows 43-46 (L 216-240) end in a dark row 47 (L 44) that works as the eave shadow, then the brick front face with windows starts. The step from green (L~115) to cornice (L~230) is well over 25 L. The roof is tall for a foreshortened top, but the vents and parapet make it read clearly as a roof seen from above, with a separate front face below. The windows have sills and lintels, and the door is set in an arch.

style.evidence: The candidate has 13 median colours per tile, against 18 and 11 for the references, and 0% flat-fill coverage. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark red-brown or green. It has 42 distinct colours, fewer than the references (185 and 66), but the brick has several tones, mortar lines and per-brick speckle, and the windows have frames, glass highlights and sills. The green roof repeats a tile-like pattern with three greens, which is a little regular. It would sit acceptably next to the references.
